newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey asks U.S. to look into Kurdish institute.
newsitem.headline: Turkey asks U.S. to look into Kurdish institute.

text.p: Turkey has asked NATO ally the United States to investigate a Kurdish institute in Washington allegedly run by Kurdish rebels fighting for self rule in Turkey, the foreign ministry said on Wednesday.
"We expect a serious investigation from the U.S. authorities on the subject including (the institute's) financial sources and other connections," ministry spokesman Omer Akbel told a news briefing.
The name of the institute was not given.
Rebel leader Abdullah Ocalan was quoted by a Turkish newspaper this week as saying that the institute was run by his Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) guerrilla group.
"We are making official initiatives (to the United States)," Akbel said.

More than 21,000 people have been killed in a 12-year-old conflict between security forces and PKK rebels in the mainly-Kurdish southeast of Turkey. Turkey says many legal Kurdish organisations abroad act as front groups for the rebels.
